provisions.applies_to: All physical goods except the listed categories
provisions.conditions: Being in scope creates no DPP duty by itself; duties arise through Art. 4 delegated acts.

provisions.summary: 'Digital product passport' is a product-specific data set that includes the information specified in the applicable Art. 4 delegated act and is accessible electronically through a data carrier in accordance with Chapter III.
provisions.applies_to: Definition
provisions.conditions: The definition is tied to an Art. 4 delegated act: by its wording it does not cover passports created under other Union acts.

provisions.summary: Definitions: data carrier (linear barcode, two-dimensional symbol or other automatic identification data capture medium readable by a device); unique product identifier (unique character string identifying a product that also enables a web link to the DPP); unique operator identifier (string identifying an actor in the value chain); DPP service provider (natural or legal person that is an independent third party authorised by the economic operator placing the product on the market or putting it into service, and that processes DPP data to make it available to operators and other actors with access rights under this Regulation or other Union law); unique facility identifier (string identifying locations or buildings in the value chain).
provisions.applies_to: Definitions
provisions.conditions: None

provisions.summary: 'Economic operator' means the manufacturer, authorised representative, importer, distributor, dealer and fulfilment service provider. DPP service providers are not listed as economic operators.
provisions.applies_to: Definition of obligated actor class
provisions.conditions: None

provisions.summary: Empowers the Commission to adopt delegated acts under Art. 72 setting ecodesign requirements; they must contain at least the Art. 8 elements and be set in accordance with Arts 5, 6, 7 and Chapter III (the DPP chapter).
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: Art. 4(3): no delegated act may state that no ecodesign requirements are necessary for a product group.

provisions.summary: The date of application of an Art. 4 delegated act must not be earlier than 18 months after its entry into force.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; every Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Exceptions: duly justified cases (whole act or specific requirements) and partial repeal or amendment of delegated acts, where an earlier date may be set.

provisions.summary: The first delegated act adopted under Art. 4 shall not enter into force before 19 July 2025.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: Combined with Art. 4(4), the earliest ordinary date of application of any Art. 4 requirement would have been 18 months after 19 July 2025; no Art. 4 act located as adopted.

provisions.summary: Information requirements in delegated acts must include, as a minimum, requirements related to the DPP set out in Chapter III and requirements on substances of concern. Where a delegated act contains horizontal ecodesign requirements, point (a) does not apply.
provisions.applies_to: Commission when drafting Art. 4 delegated acts; indirectly products covered
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: adoption and application of an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Not applicable to delegated acts containing horizontal requirements; Art. 9(4) allows exemption of product groups from the DPP.

provisions.summary: Where a DPP is available, the required information must be provided in it and, where necessary, also on the product, its packaging, a label, a manual or a free-access website or application. Information for tracking substances of concern must be on the product or accessible through a data carrier on the product.
provisions.applies_to: Products covered by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Depends on the information requirements set in the delegated act.

provisions.summary: The information requirements must provide that products can only be placed on the market or put into service if a DPP is available in accordance with the applicable Art. 4 delegated acts and with Arts 10 and 11. DPP data must be accurate, complete and up to date.
provisions.applies_to: Products covered by an Art. 4 delegated act; economic operators placing them on the market
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act (none located as adopted on 2026-10-13)
provisions.conditions: Wholly dependent on a product-specific delegated act; Art. 9(4) exemptions possible.

provisions.summary: Each delegated act must specify, as appropriate for the product group: (a) DPP data pursuant to Annex III; (b) data carrier(s); (c) layout and positioning of the data carrier; (d) model, batch or item level and their definitions; (e) how the DPP is made accessible to customers before a contract, including distance selling; (f) which actors access which data; (g) which actors may create or update which data; (h) arrangements for introducing or updating data; (i) the availability period, at least the expected lifetime of the specific product.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; content of each Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: These nine items are not fixed by the ESPR itself; an engine cannot test them for ESPR products until a delegated act exists.

provisions.summary: The Art. 9(2) requirements must ensure that value-chain actors can easily access and understand relevant product information, facilitate verification of compliance by competent national authorities, and improve traceability.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; DPP requirements in delegated acts
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: Objectives clause.

provisions.summary: The Commission may exempt product groups from the DPP requirement where (a) technical specifications for the DPP are not available in relation to the essential requirements of Arts 10 and 11, or (b) other Union law includes a system for the digital provision of product-group information that the Commission considers achieves the objectives of Art. 9(3)(a) and (b).
provisions.applies_to: Commission; product groups
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: Point (b) names no specific Union act; it does not mention the Batteries Regulation.

provisions.summary: A DPP must be connected through a data carrier to a persistent unique product identifier; the data carrier must be physically present on the product, its packaging or accompanying documentation, as the delegated act specifies.
provisions.applies_to: Digital product passports under the ESPR
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Placement is set by the delegated act.

provisions.summary: The data carrier and the unique product identifier must comply with one or more of the standards named in Annex III, second paragraph, or equivalent European or international standards, until the references of harmonised standards are published in the Official Journal.
provisions.applies_to: Data carriers and unique product identifiers of ESPR DPPs
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Time-limited fallback. References of harmonised standards on unique identifiers and data carriers (EN 18219:2026, EN 18220:2026) were published in the OJ on 2026-07-15 by Decision (EU) 2026/1736; the legal effect on this fallback is an open interpretation question.

provisions.citation: Art. 10(1) point (d) (as corrected by corrigendum R(02))
provisions.summary: All DPP data must be based on open standards, developed with an interoperable format, and be, as appropriate, machine-readable, structured, searchable and transferable through an open interoperable data exchange network without vendor lock-in.
provisions.applies_to: All data in ESPR DPPs
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: In accordance with the essential requirements of Arts 10 and 11.

provisions.summary: Personal data relating to customers must not be stored in the DPP without their explicit consent in compliance with Art. 6 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679.
provisions.applies_to: ESPR DPPs; operators and service providers storing DPP data
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Explicit consent exception.

provisions.summary: DPP data must refer to the product model, batch or item as specified in the delegated act; access to DPP data is regulated by the essential requirements of Arts 10 and 11 and by the product-group access rights specified in the delegated act.
provisions.applies_to: ESPR DPPs
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: Granularity and access rights are set only by the delegated act.

provisions.summary: The Commission may, by delegated act under Art. 72, amend Annex III first paragraph point (c) and second paragraph by replacing or adding European or international standards for data carriers, unique operator identifiers and unique facility identifiers.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: In light of technical and scientific progress. No such amending act located.

provisions.summary: Where other Union law requires or allows the inclusion of specific data in the DPP, those data may be included in the DPP pursuant to the applicable Art. 4 delegated act.
provisions.applies_to: Data from other Union law
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: Generic reference to other Union law; no act named; operates through an Art. 4 delegated act.

provisions.summary: The economic operator placing the product on the market must give dealers and online marketplace providers a digital copy of the data carrier or the unique product identifier so that it can be shown to potential customers who cannot physically access the product, and must provide that copy or a webpage link free of charge, promptly and in any event within five working days of a request.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the product on the market
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Threshold: five working days from receipt of the request.

provisions.summary: When placing the product on the market, the economic operator must make available a back-up copy of the DPP through a DPP service provider.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the product on the market
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Requirements for service providers themselves await the Art. 11 delegated act (not adopted as far as located).

provisions.summary: Essential requirements for technical design and operation: (a) full interoperability with other DPPs required by Art. 4 delegated acts on technical, semantic and organisational aspects of end-to-end communication and data transfer; (b) free and easy access for customers, manufacturers, importers, distributors, dealers, professional repairers, independent operators, refurbishers, remanufacturers, recyclers, market surveillance and customs authorities, civil society organisations, trade unions and other relevant actors, according to their access rights in the delegated act; (c) storage by the economic operator responsible for creation or by DPP service providers; (d) a new DPP for a product that already has one must be linked to the original(s); (e) availability for the period set in the delegated act, including after insolvency, liquidation or cessation of Union activity of the responsible operator; (f) rights to introduce, modify or update data restricted according to access rights in delegated acts; (g) data authentication, reliability and integrity ensured; (h) design and operation ensuring a high level of security and privacy and avoiding fraud.
provisions.applies_to: ESPR DPP systems; economic operator responsible for the DPP; DPP service providers
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Points (a), (b), (e), (f) depend on content of delegated acts. Presumption of conformity through harmonised standards cited in the OJ (Art. 41(2)).

provisions.summary: DPP service providers that store or otherwise process the DPP must not sell, reuse or process the data, in whole or in part, beyond what is necessary for the storing or processing service.
provisions.applies_to: DPP service providers
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Unless specifically agreed with the economic operator placing the product on the market or putting it into service.

provisions.summary: Empowers the Commission to adopt delegated acts under Art. 72 setting the requirements DPP service providers must meet to become such providers, where appropriate a certification scheme to verify them, and requirements for providing DPP services.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; future DPP service providers
provisions.applicable_from: 2024-07-18 (empowerment); obligations only once a delegated act applies
provisions.conditions: No deadline in the text. No adopted act located; Commission plans Q2-Q3 2027.

provisions.summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts (examination procedure, Art. 73(3)) on procedures to issue and verify digital credentials of economic operators and other actors with access rights to DPP data.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: Optional; none located.

provisions.summary: Unique operator identifiers (Annex III first paragraph points (g) and (h)) and unique facility identifiers (point (i)) must comply with the standards named in Annex III first paragraph point (c) and second paragraph, or equivalent European or international standards, until references of harmonised standards are published in the Official Journal.
provisions.applies_to: Unique operator and facility identifiers in ESPR DPPs
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Same time-limited fallback as Art. 10(1)(c).

provisions.summary: Where a unique operator identifier (other than the manufacturer's) or a unique facility identifier is not yet available, the economic operator that creates or updates the DPP must request one on behalf of the relevant actor, after first seeking that actor's confirmation that none exists, and must give the actor full details of the identifier once issued.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator that creates or updates the DPP
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Prior confirmation step required.

provisions.summary: Empowers the Commission to adopt delegated acts on life cycle management of unique identifiers and data carriers: rules for organisations wishing to become issuing agencies and for economic operators creating their own identifiers and data carriers without an issuing agency. The acts must set criteria and role of issuing agencies, rules ensuring identifiers and carriers are reliable, verifiable and globally unique, rules on creating, maintaining, updating and withdrawing them, and data management rules. The Commission must seek interoperability between approaches, take account of existing technical solutions and standards, and stay technologically neutral as far as possible.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; issuing agencies; economic operators self-issuing identifiers
provisions.applicable_from: 2024-07-18 (empowerment)
provisions.conditions: No adopted or draft act located.

provisions.citation: Art. 13(1) first, second and fourth subparagraphs
provisions.summary: By 19 July 2026 the Commission must set up a digital registry that securely stores at least the unique identifiers; for products intended for the customs procedure 'release for free circulation' the registry must also store the commodity code. The Commission manages the registry and must ensure secure processing compliant with Union law including personal data rules.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.applicable_from: 2026-07-19 (deadline)
provisions.conditions: Commission news states the registry went live on 2026-07-20; this audit did not contact the registry.

provisions.citation: Art. 13(1) third subparagraph [ESPR to Batteries cross-reference]
provisions.summary: The registry must store the unique identifiers for batteries referred to in Art. 77(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. Effect: it extends the content of the ESPR registry to battery unique identifiers. It does not make any other ESPR DPP provision applicable to battery passports.
provisions.applies_to: Commission (registry content); battery unique identifiers under Art. 77(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542
provisions.applicable_from: 2026-07-19 (registry deadline)
provisions.conditions: The matching upload duty for operators is in Art. 77(10) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, inserted by Art. 78 ESPR.

provisions.summary: In Art. 4 delegated acts the Commission must specify any other data that, besides being in the DPP, must be stored in the registry, considering verification of DPP authenticity, usefulness for market surveillance and customs controls, and avoiding disproportionate administrative burden.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; registry data per product group
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: Additional registry data is product-specific and not yet defined for any ESPR product group.

provisions.summary: For setting up and managing the registry and any resulting personal data processing, the Commission is regarded as controller under Art. 3(8) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.conditions: None

provisions.summary: The economic operator placing the product on the market or putting it into service must upload to the registry the data referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing the product on the market or putting it into service
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: registry operational and product covered by an obligation to have a DPP
provisions.conditions: No explicit deadline in the paragraph. Detailed arrangements: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778.

provisions.summary: After upload the registry automatically communicates to the operator a unique registration identifier associated with the uploaded unique identifiers; that communication is not proof of compliance with the Regulation or other Union law. The Commission must adopt an implementing act (examination procedure, Art. 73(3)) on implementation arrangements for the registry, including communication of the registration identifier.
provisions.applies_to: Registry (Commission); economic operators
provisions.applicable_from: 2024-07-18; implementing act adopted 2026-07-16 as Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778
provisions.conditions: No deadline for the implementing act in the text.

provisions.summary: The Commission, competent national authorities and customs authorities have access to the registry for their duties under Union law.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; competent national authorities; customs authorities
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: registry operational
provisions.conditions: The paragraph grants registry access to authorities only; it grants none to the public or to economic operators.

provisions.summary: The Commission must set up and manage a publicly accessible web portal allowing stakeholders to search for and compare DPP data consistently with their access rights under Art. 4 delegated acts.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.applicable_from: 2024-07-18 (no deadline)
provisions.conditions: No date set; status of the portal not established in this audit.

provisions.summary: Any person intending to place a product covered by an Art. 4 delegated act under 'release for free circulation' must provide or make available to customs the unique registration identifier of Art. 13(5). Applies from the moment the registry is operational.
provisions.applies_to: Declarant/importer of products covered by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: registry operational AND product covered by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: By its wording limited to products covered by an Art. 4 delegated act; batteries are not covered by this wording (consistent with Commission batteries FAQ Q4.1).

provisions.summary: Customs may release a product for free circulation only after verifying at least that the unique registration identifier and the commodity code correspond to the registry data; the verification is electronic and automatic via the Art. 15(3) interconnection and applies from the moment the interconnection is operational. Release is not proof of compliance.
provisions.applies_to: Customs authorities
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: interconnection with EU CSW-CERTEX operational
provisions.conditions: Depends on Art. 15(3).

provisions.summary: The Commission must interconnect the registry with the EU Customs Single Window Certificates Exchange System (EU CSW-CERTEX) under Regulation (EU) 2022/2399; the interconnection must be operational within four years of the entry into force of the Art. 13(5) implementing act.
provisions.applies_to: Commission
provisions.applicable_from: Deadline computed as 2030-08-06 (four years after computed entry into force of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778)
provisions.conditions: Computed date; depends on the entry-into-force date of Regulation (EU) 2026/1778.

provisions.summary: The Commission and customs authorities may retrieve and use DPP and registry data for their Union-law duties, including risk management, customs controls and release under Regulation (EU) No 952/2013. The Article is without prejudice to that Regulation, Chapter VII of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and other Union law.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; customs authorities
provisions.conditions: None

provisions.summary: When setting label information requirements, the Commission must, where appropriate, require the label to include data carriers or other means giving customers access to additional product information, including access to the DPP.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; labels required by delegated acts
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: Where appropriate.

provisions.summary: When placing products covered by an Art. 4 delegated act on the market or putting them into service, manufacturers must ensure that a DPP is available in accordance with Art. 9 and the delegated act, including a back-up copy of the most up-to-date version stored by a DPP service provider in accordance with Art. 10(4).
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Art. 28(1): the Art. 27(1) obligations cannot be part of an authorised representative's mandate.

provisions.summary: Manufacturers and importers must indicate their name, registered trade name or trade mark, postal address and electronic means of contact on the public part of the DPP, where applicable, and on the product (or packaging or accompanying document).
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers; importers
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: 'Where applicable' for the DPP location.

provisions.summary: Manufacturers must include the digital instructions in the DPP and make them accessible through the corresponding data carrier (or, where no DPP applies, indicate how to access them); the instructions must be downloadable and remain accessible online during the expected lifetime of the product and in any event at least 10 years after placing on the market or putting into service.
provisions.applies_to: Manufacturers (importers and distributors by reference, Arts 29(4), 30(2)(b))
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Threshold: at least 10 years online availability; paper copy on request within one month (fifth subparagraph).

provisions.summary: Before placing a product covered by an Art. 4 delegated act on the market, importers must ensure that a DPP is available in accordance with Art. 9 and the delegated act, including a back-up copy of the most up-to-date version stored by a DPP service provider under Art. 10(4).
provisions.applies_to: Importers
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: None beyond the delegated act.

provisions.summary: Before making a covered product available, distributors must verify that it bears the CE marking or the alternative conformity marking and, where relevant, is labelled or is linked to a DPP in accordance with the delegated act.
provisions.applies_to: Distributors
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: 'Where relevant'.

provisions.summary: Dealers must ensure that the DPP is easily accessible to customers and potential customers, including in distance selling, as set out in Art. 9(2)(e) and specified in the applicable delegated act.
provisions.applies_to: Dealers
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: application date of the applicable Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Manner defined by the delegated act.

provisions.summary: DPPs that conform to harmonised standards, or parts of them, whose references have been published in the Official Journal are presumed to conform to the requirements of Arts 10 and 11 to the extent those requirements are covered by the standards.
provisions.applies_to: ESPR DPPs; harmonised standards cited in the OJ
provisions.applicable_from: From OJ publication of the references (six references published 2026-07-15 by Decision (EU) 2026/1736)
provisions.conditions: Presumption limited to requirements covered; standards are voluntary means of compliance.

provisions.summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts establishing common specifications covering, among others, the essential requirements for DPPs in Arts 10 and 11, but only where a standardisation request was not accepted, not delivered on time or the standard does not comply, and no reference is published in the OJ or expected within a reasonable period. Conformity with such common specifications gives a presumption of conformity to the extent covered.
provisions.applies_to: Commission; ESPR DPPs
provisions.conditions: Cumulative conditions in Art. 42(1)(a) and (b); none located as adopted.

provisions.citation: Art. 78 (as corrected by corrigendum R(01)) [ESPR to Batteries cross-reference]
provisions.version_examined: 02024R1781-20240628 (EN 000.001), PDF p. 75, marker C1; original OJ text also read
provisions.summary: Amends Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 by adding paragraph 10 to its Art. 77: the economic operator placing the battery on the market or putting it into service must upload the unique identifier in the registry referred to in Art. 13(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781. Effect: creates, inside the Batteries Regulation, a single ESPR-linked duty (registry upload of the battery unique identifier). It does not make ESPR Arts 9 to 12, 14 or 15 applicable to battery passports.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operator placing a battery on the market or putting it into service (battery categories of Art. 77(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542)
provisions.applicable_from: Amendment in force 2024-07-18; the inserted paragraph contains no date of its own. The battery passport duty of Art. 77(1) starts 2027-02-18.
provisions.conditions: The original OJ wording cited 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1726'; corrected to 2024/1781 by corrigendum OJ L, 2024/90493 of 7.8.2024.

provisions.summary: Replaces point (27) of Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828 (representative actions) with a reference to Regulation (EU) 2024/1781.
provisions.applies_to: Directive (EU) 2020/1828 Annex I
provisions.conditions: Not DPP-specific.

provisions.summary: Directive 2009/125/EC is repealed with effect from 18 July 2024, except that listed provisions continue to apply until 31 December 2026 for listed energy-related product groups and until 31 December 2030 for products regulated by implementing measures under Art. 15 of the Directive (insofar as amendments address technical issues), and further listed provisions continue for products regulated by such implementing measures until those are repealed or declared obsolete. References to the repealed Directive are construed as references to this Regulation per Annex VIII. Manufacturers of products placed on the market under the Directive before an Art. 4 delegated act applies must keep an electronic version of conformity documentation for 10 years and produce it within 10 days of a request.
provisions.applies_to: Products under Directive 2009/125/EC implementing measures; manufacturers
provisions.conditions: Art. 79(3) means recitals 37 and 38 of the Batteries Regulation, which refer to Directive 2009/125/EC, are now read as references to the ESPR (general construction rule, not a battery-specific mapping).

provisions.summary: The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal and is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States. The Article contains no calendar date and no deferred date of application.
provisions.applies_to: Whole Regulation
provisions.applicable_from: 2024-07-18 (computed from publication on 2024-06-28)
provisions.conditions: None

provisions.summary: Menu from which delegated acts specify what data are to be or can be included in the DPP: (a) information required under Art. 7(2)(b) and Art. 7(5) or other Union law applicable to the product group; (b) unique product identifier at the level set in the delegated act; (c) Global Trade Identification Number as provided for in ISO/IEC 15459-6 or equivalent; (d) relevant commodity codes such as a TARIC code; (e) compliance documentation such as declaration of conformity, technical documentation or conformity certificates; (f) user manuals, instructions, warnings or safety information required by other Union law; (g) manufacturer information including its unique operator identifier; (h) unique operator identifiers other than the manufacturer's; (i) unique facility identifiers; (j) importer information including EORI number; (k) name, contact details and unique operator identifier of the Union-established economic operator responsible under Art. 4 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 or Art. 15 of Regulation (EU) 2023/988; (l) reference of the DPP service provider hosting the back-up copy.
provisions.applies_to: Commission (content of delegated acts); ESPR DPP data model
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: each delegated act
provisions.conditions: Annex III is a menu, not a mandatory data set; the binding data set per product group comes only from the delegated act. Annex III does not mention batteries.

provisions.summary: The data carrier, the unique product identifier, the unique operator identifiers of points (g), (h) and (k) and the unique facility identifiers of point (i) must, where relevant for the products concerned, comply with ISO/IEC 15459-1:2014, ISO/IEC 15459-2:2015, ISO/IEC 15459-3:2014, ISO/IEC 15459-4:2014, ISO/IEC 15459-5:2014 and ISO/IEC 15459-6:2014 (standard numbers and years as written in the Regulation; no standard content consulted).
provisions.applies_to: Data carriers and identifiers of ESPR DPPs
provisions.applicable_from: Condition: a DPP required by an Art. 4 delegated act
provisions.conditions: Read with Arts 10(1)(c) and 12(1): applies until references of harmonised standards are published in the OJ; equivalent European or international standards allowed; Annex amendable by delegated act (Art. 10(1) second subparagraph). A third paragraph of Annex III on additional information that manufacturers may include was reported by one extractor read and not checked on the PDF page.

provisions.citation: Art. 77(10) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 [Batteries to ESPR cross-reference]
provisions.summary: The economic operator placing the battery on the market or putting it into service must upload the unique identifier in the registry referred to in Art. 13(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781. This is the only provision of the Batteries Regulation that names the ESPR by number.
provisions.applies_to: Economic operators placing on the market or putting into service batteries that need a battery passport under Art. 77(1)
provisions.applicable_from: No date in the paragraph. Read with Art. 77(1): battery passport from 2027-02-18; read with Art. 13(1) ESPR: registry due 2026-07-19.
provisions.conditions: Covers the unique identifier only. Registration mechanics: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Arts 1(1)(b) and 8.

provisions.citation: Art. 78 point (a) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 [Batteries to ecodesign law cross-reference]
provisions.version_examined: OJ L 191, 28.7.2023 and consolidated 13.08.2026 (no amendment marker on Art. 78)
provisions.summary: The battery passport must be fully interoperable with other digital product passports required by Union law concerning eco-design, as regards technical, semantic and organisational aspects of end-to-end communication and data transfer. Generic wording adopted before the ESPR existed: it does not cite Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 and it imposes an interoperability property on the battery passport; it does not import ESPR obligations.
provisions.applies_to: Battery passport technical design and operation
provisions.applicable_from: With the battery passport duty: 2027-02-18
provisions.conditions: Mirror clause of Art. 11(a) ESPR, which requires interoperability only with DPPs required by Art. 4 delegated acts (not with battery passports).

provisions.citation: Art. 77(1), (3) and (9) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (context for the cross-references)
provisions.summary: From 18 February 2027 each LMT battery, industrial battery with capacity above 2 kWh and electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service must have an electronic record (battery passport). The passport is accessible through the QR code linked to a unique identifier attributed by the economic operator placing the battery on the market; QR code and identifier must comply with the ISO/IEC 15459 parts 1 to 6 named there.
